question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of the coffee-chain café market in the United States?
hint_en: Start from US adults who buy café coffee, multiply by visits per week and spend per visit, then annualize. Coffee drinkers vs. chain buyers is the first split.
referenceStats: US adults ~250M; ~40% are regular chain-café buyers (~100M) buying ~2 cups/week at ~$5 each → ~100M × 2 × 52 × $5 ≈ $52B. Cross-check vs. Starbucks US revenue (~$25B) as roughly half the chain segment → order of tens of billions.
anchor: US population ~330M; ~250M adults; coffee a daily habit for many

question_en: How many ride-hailing drivers are actively on the road at 6pm on a typical weekday across the United States?
hint_en: Estimate concurrent ride demand (rides happening at once) from daily rides ÷ active hours, then convert to drivers using utilization. Demand-side first, then supply.
referenceStats: US ride-hailing ~20M rides/day; evening peak ~8% in the busy hour → ~1.6M rides/hour; each ride ~15 min so ~0.4M rides in progress at any instant; with ~50% driver utilization at peak → ~0.8M drivers online. Order of magnitude: high hundreds of thousands.
anchor: US population ~330M; large metros ~1–10M people; a ride lasts ~15 min

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of a single busy urban fast-food restaurant?
hint_en: Build from transactions per hour during peak and off-peak, average ticket, and operating hours per day, then annualize over operating days.
referenceStats: ~12 operating hours: ~4 peak hours at ~60 orders/hr + ~8 off-peak at ~20/hr → ~400 orders/day × $10 ticket = $4,000/day × 360 days ≈ $1.4M/year. Cross-check: typical US QSR unit does ~$1–3M/year, so this sits at the lower-mid end.
anchor: A fast-food outlet seats few but turns fast; lunch+dinner peaks; ticket ~$10

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of the haircut and salon services market in the United States, estimated both top-down and bottom-up?
hint_en: Bottom-up: people × cuts/year × price. Top-down: number of salons × revenue per salon. Reconcile the two and explain the gap.
referenceStats: Bottom-up: ~280M people getting ~6 cuts/year at ~$25 avg ≈ $42B. Top-down: ~1M salons/barbershops × ~$50–60K revenue per chair-equivalent slice → tens of billions. Both converge on ~$45–55B; the gap comes from color/treatment upsell and tips not captured in the bottom-up price.
anchor: US ~330M people; haircut every ~5–8 weeks; ~$25 average cut

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of the pet food market in the United States?
hint_en: Households with pets × pets per household × annual food spend per pet. Split dogs vs. cats since spend per animal differs.
referenceStats: ~85M households own pets; ~90M dogs at ~$300/yr food + ~75M cats at ~$200/yr food ≈ $27B + $15B ≈ $42B. Cross-check vs. total US pet industry (~$150B incl. vet/supplies); food is ~30% → ~$45B. Order: ~$40–50B.
anchor: US ~130M households; pets in ~65% of homes; food bag bought monthly

question_en: How many people are watching a major video-streaming platform (e.g., a Netflix-scale service) simultaneously during global prime time?
hint_en: Start from subscriber base, daily active share, average daily watch time, then convert to concurrency at the global peak hour accounting for time zones.
referenceStats: ~250M subscriber accounts × ~1.5 viewers/account = ~375M potential viewers; ~50% watch on a given day for ~2 hrs each. After time-zone smoothing the single highest instant ≈ 20–30M concurrent streams. Order: tens of millions.
anchor: Global population ~8B; ~5B internet users; video streaming dominates traffic

question_en: How many gallons of gasoline are sold for passenger vehicles in the United States per year?
hint_en: Vehicles × annual miles driven × average fuel economy (miles per gallon). Use passenger cars/light trucks only.
referenceStats: ~250M light-duty vehicles × ~12,000 miles/yr ÷ ~25 mpg ≈ 120B gallons. Cross-check: US motor gasoline consumption is ~135B gallons/yr including all light vehicles → order of ~10^11 gallons.
anchor: US ~330M; ~230M licensed drivers; ~290M registered vehicles

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of a single 120-room mid-scale hotel running at typical occupancy?
hint_en: Rooms × occupancy × average daily rate × 365 for room revenue, then add a markup for food/beverage and other services.
referenceStats: 120 rooms × 70% occupancy × $120 ADR × 365 ≈ $3.7M room revenue; add ~25% for F&B/other → ~$4.6M total. Cross-check: RevPAR ≈ $84 × 120 × 365 ≈ $3.7M confirms the room line.
anchor: A mid-scale hotel ~120 rooms; ADR ~$120; occupancy ~70%

question_en: How many smartphones are sold worldwide per year, estimated top-down and bottom-up?
hint_en: Bottom-up: installed base ÷ replacement cycle + new first-time buyers. Top-down: regional populations × penetration × turnover. Reconcile.
referenceStats: Bottom-up: ~4.5B installed base ÷ ~3.5-yr replacement ≈ 1.3B replacements + ~0.1B net new users ≈ 1.3–1.4B/yr. Top-down by region (Asia/EU/Americas) lands ~1.2–1.4B. Both converge near ~1.2B units/year. Order: ~10^9.
anchor: Global ~8B; ~5.5B mobile phone users; phones replaced ~every 3 yrs

question_en: How many food-delivery orders are placed through apps in the United States on a typical Friday evening (5–9pm)?
hint_en: Estimate ordering households in metros, the share that orders delivery on a peak Friday, and confine it to the 4-hour dinner window.
referenceStats: ~80M metro/suburban households with delivery access; ~8% order on a busy Friday night → ~6.4M orders concentrated in the 5–9pm window. Cross-check vs. ~3M average daily US delivery orders, with Friday peak hours running several-fold above the daily-average hourly rate → low-millions in the window.
anchor: US ~130M households; ~95% have internet; food delivery common in metros

question_en: How many disposable diapers are used in the United States per year?
hint_en: Number of children still in diapers × diaper changes per day × 365. Anchor on births per year and the years a child stays in diapers.
referenceStats: ~3.6M births/yr × ~2.5 years in diapers ≈ 9M children in diapers; ~6 diapers/day × 365 → ~9M × 2,190 ≈ 20B diapers/year. Order: ~2 × 10^10.
anchor: US ~330M; ~3.6M births/yr; diapers used for ~2.5 yrs

question_en: What annual recurring revenue (USD) does a B2B SaaS startup reach 3 years after launch if it adds 200 paying customers per month at 2% monthly churn?
hint_en: Track the customer base month over month: additions minus churn compound into a partially-saturated base, then multiply by annual revenue per customer.
referenceStats: Net base with 200 adds/mo and 2% monthly churn approaches equilibrium near adds ÷ churn = 200 ÷ 0.02 = 10,000, but at 36 months it's still ramping → ~5,500 customers. × $50/mo × 12 ≈ $3.3M ARR. Order: low single-digit millions ARR.
anchor: A SaaS startup; ARPU ~$50/mo; churn ~2%/mo; 200 adds/mo

question_en: How many airline passenger seats are sold (passenger boardings) worldwide per year?
hint_en: Start from annual passengers (trips, not unique people), or build from aircraft fleet × seats × flights/day × load factor. Cross-check the two.
referenceStats: Build-up: ~25,000 commercial passenger jets × ~3 flights/day × ~180 seats × ~80% load × 360 days ≈ 3.9B passenger-trips. Cross-check: industry reports ~4–4.5B passenger boardings/year → order of ~4 × 10^9 seats sold.
anchor: Global ~8B; ~25,000 commercial passenger jets; ~180 seats/plane

question_en: How many messages are sent across the world's largest messaging platform during its single busiest minute of the year?
hint_en: Annual or daily message volume → average per second, then apply a peak multiplier for an event (e.g., New Year) when many time zones celebrate at once.
referenceStats: ~2B users × ~40 messages/day ≈ 80B/day ≈ 0.9M/sec average. New Year's-style peaks run ~30–50× average for a minute → ~30M/sec × 60 ≈ ~1.8B messages in the peak minute. Order: ~10^9 in one minute.
anchor: Global ~5B internet users; messaging near-universal; New Year peaks by zone

question_en: What is the total annual residential electricity consumption (kWh) in the United States, via household and via per-capita routes?
hint_en: Route A: households × kWh per household per year. Route B: population × per-capita residential kWh. Reconcile and note what differs.
referenceStats: Route A: ~130M households × ~10,500 kWh/yr ≈ 1,365B kWh. Route B: ~330M people × ~4,200 kWh/yr residential ≈ 1,386B kWh. Both converge near ~1.4 trillion kWh (~1.4 × 10^12). Routes agree because per-household and per-capita are linked by ~2.5 people/household.
anchor: US ~130M households; ~2.5 people/household; ~10,000 kWh/home/yr

question_en: What is the annual retail revenue (USD) of the global chocolate market?
hint_en: Population in chocolate-consuming regions × kg consumed per person per year × retail price per kg. Weight consumption heavily toward wealthier regions.
referenceStats: ~1.5B people in high-consumption regions at ~5 kg/yr + ~2B at ~1 kg/yr ≈ 9.5B kg; × ~$12/kg retail ≈ $110B. Cross-check vs. reported global chocolate market ~$100–130B → order of ~$10^11.
anchor: Global ~8B; chocolate eaten widely in wealthier regions; ~$12/kg retail

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of a single mid-size commercial fitness gym, and how many members visit per day?
hint_en: Revenue = members × monthly dues × 12, plus add-ons. Daily visits = members × the fraction who actually show up on an average day.
referenceStats: 3,000 members × $40/mo × 12 ≈ $1.44M dues; +~15% personal training/retail → ~$1.65M/yr. Daily visits: gyms rely on low attendance, ~10–18% of members visit/day → ~300–500 visits/day. Order: ~$1.5M revenue, hundreds of daily visits.
anchor: A gym ~3,000 members; dues ~$40/mo; ~10–15% visit on a given day

question_en: How many short-term-rental (e.g., Airbnb-style) listings are occupied on a peak summer Saturday night in the United States?
hint_en: Estimate total active US listings, then apply a high-season Saturday occupancy rate. Active supply first, then utilization.
referenceStats: ~1.5M active US short-term rental listings; peak-summer-Saturday occupancy ~70–80% → ~1.1M occupied. Cross-check: ~2 guests/listing → ~2.2M travelers housed that night, plausible against US summer travel volumes. Order: ~10^6 occupied listings.
anchor: US ~330M; ~1.5M active short-term-rental listings; travel peaks in summer

question_en: How many cups of coffee (all sources: home, office, café) are consumed in the United States per day?
hint_en: Coffee-drinking adults × cups per drinker per day. Anchor on the share of adults who drink coffee and typical daily cups.
referenceStats: ~250M adults × ~60% drink coffee (~150M) × ~3 cups/day ≈ 450M cups/day. Cross-check: US drinks ~400–500M cups/day per industry surveys → order of ~4–5 × 10^8 cups/day.
anchor: US ~330M; ~250M adults; ~60% drink coffee daily

question_en: What is the annual global revenue (USD) of the mobile-games market, via player route and via top-down app-store route?
hint_en: Player route: players × paying-user rate × annual spend per payer. Top-down: total consumer app-store spend × games share. Reconcile.
referenceStats: Player route: ~3.5B players × ~3% payers (~105M) × ~$800/yr per payer ≈ $84B. Top-down: app-store consumer spend ~$150B × ~60% games ≈ $90B. Both converge near ~$85–90B/yr. Order: ~$10^11.
anchor: Global ~5.5B mobile users; ~3.5B play mobile games; payers ~3%

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of a single large suburban supermarket?
hint_en: Transactions per day (customers through checkout) × average basket size × operating days. Build the customer count from peak and off-peak flow.
referenceStats: ~2,500 transactions/day × ~$35 basket ≈ $87,500/day × 360 ≈ $31M/yr. Cross-check: typical US supermarket does ~$15–40M/yr in sales, so a busy suburban unit sits in the upper range. Order: tens of millions.
anchor: A supermarket ~40,000 sq ft; ~$35 average basket; busy suburban site

question_en: How many new passenger cars and light trucks are sold in the United States per year?
hint_en: Installed fleet ÷ average vehicle lifespan gives the replacement rate; add modest fleet growth. Anchor on total registered vehicles and how long they last.
referenceStats: ~290M registered light vehicles ÷ ~18-year average lifespan ≈ 16M replacements/yr; minor net fleet growth keeps it near 15–17M. Cross-check: US new light-vehicle sales run ~15–17M/yr → order of ~10^7 units.
anchor: US ~330M; ~290M registered light vehicles; ~18-yr vehicle lifespan

question_en: How many search queries per second does the world's largest search engine handle at its global peak?
hint_en: Annual or daily query volume → average queries per second, then apply a modest peak factor since global usage smooths across time zones.
referenceStats: ~5 trillion queries/year ÷ 31.5M sec ≈ 160,000 queries/sec average. Global time-zone smoothing keeps the peak multiplier modest (~1.5–2×) → ~250,000–320,000 queries/sec at peak. Order: ~10^5 qps.
anchor: Global ~8B; one search engine handles most queries; usage spread by waking hours

question_en: What is the annual global box-office revenue (USD) for cinema?
hint_en: Cinema-going population × tickets per person per year × average ticket price, weighted toward regions with strong theater habits.
referenceStats: ~2B regular cinema-goers × ~2 tickets/yr × ~$7 avg global ticket ≈ $28B; add occasional viewers → ~$30–40B. Cross-check vs. reported global box office (~$30–40B) → order of ~$10^10.
anchor: Global ~8B; ~2B regular cinema-goers; ticket ~$7 avg globally

question_en: What is the annual revenue (USD) of a single 8-stall EV fast-charging station at a busy highway location, and what stall utilization does that imply?
hint_en: Sessions/stall/day from operating hours, session length and utilization × energy or price per session × 365. Then sanity-check the implied utilization.
referenceStats: 8 stalls × ~16 active hours ÷ ~0.5 hr/session × ~40% utilization ≈ ~100 sessions/day; × ~30 kWh × ~$0.45/kWh ≈ $1,350/day × 365 ≈ $490K/yr. Cross-check: 40% utilization at a busy highway site is plausible-to-optimistic; a lower 20% utilization halves revenue to ~$250K. Order: hundreds of thousands USD.
anchor: An EV fast-charging site ~8 stalls; session ~30 min; ~30 kWh/session

question_en: How many pizzas are sold worldwide in a single day?
hint_en: Start from the major pizza-eating regions (US + Europe as the core), estimate slices or pies per person per week, then convert to a daily, global figure. The US alone is a useful anchor before scaling out.
referenceStats: US population ~330M; ~1 pizza per person per week in the US (~3 billion pizzas/year ≈ ~8M/day in the US). Scale up ~2–3× for Europe + rest of world heavy markets → roughly 20–30M pizzas/day globally.
anchor: US population ~330M; world population ~8B

question_en: How many personal computers (desktops + laptops) are shipped worldwide in one year?
hint_en: Work from the global installed base of PCs and an average replacement cycle, which is longer than for phones. Annual shipments roughly equal the active base divided by the replacement period, plus modest first-time demand.
referenceStats: Global PC installed base ~1.5–1.6B active machines; average replacement cycle ~5–6 years → ~260–300M replacement units/year; plus net new buyers keeps annual shipments around ~250–300M units.
anchor: World population ~8B; ~1.5B active PCs in use

question_en: How many cigarettes are consumed worldwide in one year?
hint_en: Estimate the global adult smoking population, then multiply by an average number of cigarettes per smoker per day and annualize. Smoking prevalence varies sharply by region.
referenceStats: World adults ~5.5B; smokers ~20% (~1.1B) at ~13–15 cigarettes/day → ~1.1B × 14 × 365 ≈ ~5.5–6 trillion cigarettes/year (commonly cited ~5.5T).
anchor: World population ~8B; ~1.1B smokers

question_en: What is the cumulative number of solar panels (PV modules) ever installed worldwide?
hint_en: Convert total installed solar capacity (in gigawatts) into module count using an average wattage per panel. Cumulative capacity, not annual additions, is what you want here.
referenceStats: Global cumulative solar capacity ~1,500 GW (~1.5 TW); average module ~0.4 kW each → ~1.5e12 W / 400 W ≈ ~3.5–4 billion modules cumulatively installed.
anchor: Global cumulative PV capacity ~1.5 TW

question_en: How many shipping containers (TEU) cross the world's oceans each year?
hint_en: Anchor on global container port throughput, then recognize that each box is handled multiple times (load, transship, unload) so port moves overstate unique voyages. Reason from trade volume per capita as a cross-check.
referenceStats: Global container port throughput ~850M–900M TEU/year of handling moves; unique laden + empty trade flows ~200–250M TEU/year. State which you mean—handling vs. shipped—since they differ ~3–4×.
anchor: Global container port throughput ~850M TEU/year

question_en: What is the global annual revenue of the bottled-water industry (USD)?
hint_en: Multiply the drinking population by liters of bottled water consumed per person per year by an average price per liter. Developed markets drive both volume and price.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; bottled-water consumers ~3–4B at ~40–50 L/person/year; price ~$0.5–1 per liter at retail → roughly $250–350B/year (commonly cited ~$300B).
anchor: World population ~8B

question_en: How many metric tons of air cargo are transported worldwide in one year?
hint_en: Anchor on global air-freight tonne-kilometers, or build from world population times an average kg of air-freighted goods per person per year. Recognize air cargo is a small but high-value slice of total freight.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; ~7–8 kg of air-freighted goods per person per year on average → ~55–65 million tonnes/year. Cross-check: industry reports ~60–65M tonnes of air cargo annually → order of ~10^7 tonnes.
anchor: World population ~8B; air cargo is a high-value freight slice

question_en: What is the total cost of running the world's data centers in electricity per year (USD)?
hint_en: Combine global data-center electricity consumption (in terawatt-hours) with an average industrial electricity price per kWh. Energy use is the dominant operating cost lever.
referenceStats: Global data-center electricity use ~350–450 TWh/year; industrial power ~$0.10–0.15/kWh → ~$40–65B/year in electricity alone. State TWh × price/kWh explicitly.
anchor: Global data-center electricity ~400 TWh/year

question_en: How many pairs of shoes are manufactured worldwide in one year?
hint_en: Use world population times an average number of new pairs bought per person per year, recognizing rich and poor regions differ several-fold in purchase rate.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; weighted average ~2.5–3 new pairs/person/year (developed ~5–7, developing ~1–2) → ~20–24 billion pairs/year (commonly cited ~22B).
anchor: World population ~8B

question_en: What is the cumulative number of automobiles (passenger cars) on the road worldwide today?
hint_en: Combine regional vehicle-ownership rates (cars per 1,000 people) with population for high-, middle-, and low-ownership regions, then sum the fleets.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; US ~800 cars/1,000, Europe ~500, China rising ~200, low-income regions <50 → weighted global fleet ~1.4–1.5 billion vehicles (cars + light trucks).
anchor: World population ~8B; US ~330M people, ~280M registered vehicles

question_en: How many emails are sent worldwide in a single day?
hint_en: Multiply the number of email users by average emails sent per user per day, but remember a large share of total volume is automated and spam, not human-typed.
referenceStats: Email users ~4.3B; human-sent ~10–15/day each ≈ ~50–65B; total including automated + spam pushes the figure to ~300–350B/day. Separate human vs. total—they differ ~5×.
anchor: Global email users ~4.3B

question_en: What is the global annual revenue of the fast-food (quick-service restaurant) industry (USD)?
hint_en: Estimate the world's regular fast-food customers, visits per person per year, and average ticket size. Developed markets dominate spend even where developing markets dominate headcount.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; regular QSR users ~2–3B at ~30–50 visits/year × ~$7 ticket → roughly $600–900B/year (industry estimates ~$700–900B).
anchor: World population ~8B

question_en: How many barrels of oil does the world consume in a single day?
hint_en: Anchor on world population and a weighted per-capita oil consumption, recognizing the US consumes far more per person than the global average. Cross-check against the well-known global daily figure.
referenceStats: US ~330M people use ~20M barrels/day (~0.06 bbl/person/day); world average is far lower → global consumption ~100M barrels/day (a standard reference figure).
anchor: World population ~8B; US oil use ~20M bbl/day

question_en: What is the cumulative number of credit and debit cards in circulation worldwide?
hint_en: Estimate the banked adult population, then multiply by an average number of payment cards held per person, which is several in developed markets and near zero in unbanked regions.
referenceStats: World adults ~5.5B; banked share ~75% → ~4B card-holders; developed holders carry ~3–4 cards, others ~1 → cumulative ~20–24 billion cards in circulation.
anchor: World population ~8B; banked adults ~4B+

question_en: How many cups (servings) of tea are consumed worldwide in a single day?
hint_en: Tea is concentrated in Asia, the Middle East, and the UK, so weight those regions heavily for cups per person per day rather than using a flat global average.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; heavy-tea regions (~4B people) at ~2–3 cups/day plus lighter regions → roughly ~6–9 billion servings/day (tea is the second-most consumed beverage after water).
anchor: World population ~8B

question_en: What is the global annual revenue of the pet-care market (food + vet + supplies, USD)?
hint_en: Combine the number of pet-owning households in developed regions with annual spend per pet, since spending is overwhelmingly concentrated in high-income markets.
referenceStats: US pet market alone ~$120–140B; other major developed markets (Europe, etc.) add a comparable amount → global pet care roughly ~$250–300B/year.
anchor: US population ~330M; US pet market ~$130B

question_en: How many flights (commercial aircraft departures) take off worldwide in a single day?
hint_en: Work backward from annual global passengers and an average passengers-per-flight figure to get flights per year, then divide by 365. Distinguish passenger flights from cargo/private.
referenceStats: Global air passengers ~4.5B/year ÷ ~120 passengers/flight ≈ ~38M flights/year ≈ ~100,000 commercial passenger departures/day (often cited ~100k–130k including all flight types).
anchor: Global annual air passengers ~4.5B

question_en: What is the annual operating cost of the global postal and parcel-delivery 'last mile' (USD)?
hint_en: Estimate annual parcels delivered worldwide times an average last-mile cost per parcel, recognizing last mile is the costliest delivery segment per item.
referenceStats: Global parcels ~150–160B/year; last-mile cost ~$2–4/parcel (it is ~40–50% of total shipping cost) → roughly $400–600B/year in last-mile spend.
anchor: Global annual parcel volume ~150B

question_en: How many liters of milk are produced worldwide in one year?
hint_en: Anchor on world population and an average per-capita dairy-milk availability per year, weighting high-consumption regions (Europe, the Americas, South Asia) more heavily.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; weighted average ~100–110 L of milk per person/year (developed ~250+, developing far less) → ~850–900 billion liters/year (global production ~900B liters).
anchor: World population ~8B

question_en: What is the global total addressable market for online video streaming subscriptions (USD)?
hint_en: Multiply broadband-connected households worldwide by an estimated paying-subscriber rate, services per household, and average monthly fee × 12. Affordability caps adoption in lower-income regions.
referenceStats: Broadband households ~1.3B; paying SVOD households ~700–900M at ~1.8 services × ~$8/month × 12 → roughly $120–160B/year (global SVOD ~$130B+).
anchor: World broadband households ~1.3B

question_en: How many plastic bottles (PET beverage bottles) are produced worldwide in one year?
hint_en: Start from global bottled-beverage servings per person per year (water + soda) and scale by population, recognizing that one person can consume hundreds of bottles annually in heavy markets.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; ~60–70 PET bottles/person/year on average (developed markets far higher) → roughly ~480–550 billion bottles/year (commonly cited ~500B).
anchor: World population ~8B

question_en: What is the cumulative number of active bank accounts worldwide?
hint_en: Estimate the banked adult population, then multiply by an average number of accounts (checking, savings, etc.) held per banked person, which is higher in developed markets.
referenceStats: World adults ~5.5B; banked share ~75% → ~4B account-holders; developed holders average ~2–3 accounts, others ~1–1.5 → cumulative ~7–9 billion active accounts.
anchor: World population ~8B; banked adults ~4B+

question_en: What is the global annual retail revenue of the beer market (USD)?
hint_en: Combine the world's regular beer-drinking population with liters consumed per person per year and an average retail price per liter, weighting high-consumption regions and on-premise (bar) pricing.
referenceStats: World population ~8B; ~2B regular beer drinkers at ~70–80 L/year → ~150B liters; blended retail price ~$3–4/liter (cheap off-premise to expensive bar pours) → roughly $600–700B/year (global beer market often cited ~$650–750B).
anchor: World population ~8B; ~2B regular beer drinkers

question_en: How many text/chat messages (SMS + messaging apps) are sent worldwide in a single day?
hint_en: Multiply the number of messaging-app users by an average messages-sent-per-user-per-day, recognizing that app messaging volume now dwarfs traditional SMS.
referenceStats: Messaging-app users ~3B; ~30–40 sent messages/user/day → ~90–120 billion/day from one major platform alone; across all platforms total is on the order of ~100–150B/day (WhatsApp alone ~100B/day).
anchor: Global messaging-app users ~3B

question_en: What is the global annual electricity-generation revenue (utility sales to end users, USD)?
hint_en: Combine total world electricity consumption (in terawatt-hours) with an average retail price per kWh, blending cheap-power and expensive-power regions.
referenceStats: Global electricity consumption ~28,000–30,000 TWh/year; blended retail price ~$0.10–0.15/kWh → roughly $3–4 trillion/year. State TWh × price/kWh explicitly as the backbone.
anchor: World population ~8B; global electricity use ~29,000 TWh/year
